## Market-home heading: gold on the two audience terms, and no broken hyphen

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reason** | Owner direction, Jake Bennett, 17 September 2026: the heading was breaking after "Self-" and reading as "Self-" / "Employed Borrowers" across two rows. Carry "Self-Employed Borrowers" and "Business Owners" in gold and keep the first term on one line. |

| **Current staging status** | The gold terms are listed as substrings of the heading rather than as separate markup, so the heading text stays a single string and the emphasis cannot drift from the words. NOWRAP IS SCOPED. "Self-Employed Borrowers" sets about 463px wide at the heading’s smallest clamped size, so an unconditional nowrap would push the heading off a phone screen. Measured across eleven widths from 320 to 1920 to find where the phrase still fits the content column: the boundary is a little under 600px, so nowrap applies from 600 up. Both terms sit on one line from 600px upward, the heading never overflows, and below 600 the term wraps normally. REVISED the same day: "and" became an ampersand, in gold with the two terms either side. The heading is escaped before the gold terms are matched, and each term is escaped the same way before matching, so the ampersand lines up as &amp; on both sides rather than being missed or double-escaped. Re-measured at seven widths from 320 to 1440: three gold elements throughout, first term on one line down to 375, no overflow. |
| **Revert path** | Remove h1Gold from _build/home-content.js and the .dh h1 em block at the end of landing-assets/home-sections.css. |
| **Owner approval** | Owner-directed (Jake Bennett). Emphasis and line breaking only — the heading text is unchanged. |
| **Outstanding review or dependency** | None outstanding. |

## Alternative Documentation and High-Balance groups widened by 25%

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reason** | Owner direction, Jake Bennett, 17 September 2026: increase the width of those two containers by 25%. The 1x5 row in particular was running narrow cards inside the standard content column. |
| **Affected URL(s) or component(s)** | `/texas/dallas-fort-worth/ (market home)`<br>`landing-assets/home-sections.css` |
| **Current staging status** | The GROUP is widened rather than just its card grid, so the group label and its rule stay aligned with the cards beneath. Selected with :has() on the count class rather than a hand-written id, so the width survives a reorder or rebuild.

CLAMPED, BECAUSE A FLAT 25% OVERFLOWS AT EVERY COMMON WIDTH. .dh-wrap is min(1280px, 100% - 40px); a straight 125% is 1600px, wider than the 1425px of usable space in a 1440px window, and the page would have scrolled sideways. The bleed is the smaller of 125% and the viewport less a 48px gutter (which covers the scrollbar), centred by pulling half the difference back as a negative margin.

MEASURED AT SEVEN WIDTHS, sampling repeatedly while scrolling: 1920 and 1700 give the full 125% (1600px); 1440 gives 109%; 1280 and 1024 give 101%; 768 and below are unchanged because the grids have collapsed by then. Zero horizontal overflow and zero sideways scroll at every width, and the other card groups are untouched. FOLLOW-UP the same day: the owner asked to reduce the wrapping so the row covers more of the space available. Measuring first showed the obvious lever was the wrong one — at 1440 the row was already 1392px of 1425px usable, about 98%, so there was almost nothing to win outside the cards. The space was inside them: 24px of horizontal padding and a 20px gap left a five-up card’s body text 213px of a 262px card, 81%, wrapping every three or four words. Gap cut to 14px and card padding to 16px for these two groups only, and the clamp gutter from 48px to 36px. Result at 1440: text 213 -> 236px (+11%), 88% of the card, and card height 383 -> 359px from the lighter wrapping. Other card groups keep the roomier padding, which suits three-up cards. No clipped text and no overflow at 1920/1440/1280/1024/768/375. |
| **Revert path** | Delete the .dh-group:has(> .dh-card-grid-4/5) block at the end of landing-assets/home-sections.css. |
| **Owner approval** | Owner-directed (Jake Bennett). Layout only — no copy, claim or link changed. |
| **Outstanding review or dependency** | None outstanding. Worth knowing rather than reviewing: the full 25% only lands at roughly 1700px and up. At 1440, the most common desktop width, the container can only grow about 9% before it would overflow the viewport. That is a limit of the window, not a choice in the CSS. |

## GA4 reaches the Austin app: snippet on the shell, page_view on every route change

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reason** | Owner direction, Jake Bennett, 18 September 2026: add GA4 routing to the remaining page. Raised after a review-pack correction the same day found that the blocker saying no container existed was wrong, and that the real gap was one page. |
| **Affected URL(s) or component(s)** | `/`<br>`landing-assets/spa-analytics.js`<br>`_build/check-analytics-coverage.js` |
| **Current staging status** | TWENTY-FIVE OF TWENTY-SIX PAGES ALREADY REPORTED. The static Austin and DFW pages each carry the gtag snippet for G-2LMXT6BVCY in their head. /index.html, the compiled React shell, carried the Meta Pixel and no gtag, so the Austin home page was absent from GA4 outright. The snippet is now on it, copied verbatim from the other pages so there is nothing page-specific to keep in step.\n\nTHE SNIPPET ALONE WOULD HAVE MEASURED ONE PAGE PER VISIT, which is the part worth understanding before reading the reports. gtag("config") sends exactly one page_view, on document load. The app routes with wouter through history.pushState and never loads the document again, so a visitor landing on / and moving through the app would have reported their arrival and nothing after it. landing-assets/spa-analytics.js is the second half: it wraps pushState and replaceState, listens for popstate, and sends a page_view a frame after each route change, skipping the case where the path did not actually change. The entry page is never counted twice because the first change is measured against the path config already reported.\n\nSEVEN ROUTES GAIN MEASUREMENT THAT HAD NONE: /, /about, /apply, /contact, /privacy, /terms and /404. The app declares eight further route names that also exist as static pages. Which of the two a visitor gets depends on how they arrive — a fresh request to /home-loans/ is served the static file and reports through its own snippet, the same destination clicked inside the app is rendered by React and reports through this script. Both report, and they cannot both run for one navigation, so nothing is double-counted.\n\nNO QUERY STRING EVER REACHES ANALYTICS. Only location.pathname is sent, and page_location is rebuilt from origin plus pathname rather than read from href, so a campaign parameter, a CRM identifier or an address in a prefilled link cannot be written into GA4 as part of the page. Verified in the browser: pushing /about?utm_source=test&email=a%40b.com#frag reported page_path "/about" and page_location origin + "/about", with the parameters absent from the payload. The build gate refuses the file if it ever reads href, search or hash.\n\nVERIFIED LIVE, not inferred. On the running shell: gtag defined, both scripts present, history.pushState patched, and three navigations — two forward and one browser Back — produced exactly three page_view events carrying the right paths.\n\nONE LIMIT TO KNOW BEFORE READING THE REPORTS. The bundle never assigns document.title, so every app route reports the title "Leahy Lending". page_path and page_location are correct and are what to report on; the title dimension is not usable for these seven routes. Setting a title per route is a copy decision inside the app, not something a build should invent.\n\nA GATE NOW ASSERTS THE COVERAGE, because one page missing a snippet is invisible in a build log and invisible in GA4 — the property keeps reporting traffic, just not that page. check-analytics-coverage.js requires every shipped page to load and configure the same measurement ID, fails if a second property appears anywhere, and fails if the shell ever loses its route reporting. Negative-tested by removing the config line from one page. |
| **Revert path** | Remove the gtag block and the spa-analytics.js tag from /index.html, delete landing-assets/spa-analytics.js, and drop check-analytics-coverage.js from _build/build-all.js. |
| **Owner approval** | Owner-directed (Jake Bennett). Measurement only: no copy, claim, link or form field changed, and no new data is collected about a visitor beyond the page they are on. |
| **Outstanding review or dependency** | For the owner to decide before production: whether DFW should report into this same property or its own. Still outstanding from earlier entries and unaffected by this one: the §2.3 renamed events and the Super Jumbo replacement-event mapping both need reflecting in the GA4 configuration, which no build can do. For the app developer: assign document.title per route. |

## Marquee bar unified: one animation model, one speed, no gap at the loop

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reason** | Owner report, Jake Bennett, 18 September 2026: on some pages the banner moves inconsistently faster than on the DFW homepage, and it seems to run twice before a break. |
| **Affected URL(s) or component(s)** | `every DFW page`<br>`landing-assets/chrome.css`<br>`landing-assets/marquee.css`<br>`landing-assets/home-sections.css`<br>`_build/sync-marquee.js`<br>`_build/check-marquee-consistency.js` |
| **Current staging status** | BOTH SYMPTOMS WERE ONE CAUSE, AND IT WAS A PAIRING, NOT A BROKEN PART. The bar had been implemented three times — in chrome.css, in marquee.css and as a .dh-marquee block in home-sections.css — and which one a page got depended on which stylesheets it happened to link.\n\nTwo models exist and the markup decides which is right. A SINGLE RUN travels from 100vw to -100%: it enters from off-screen right, crosses, and leaves. A REPEATED RUN holds identical copies and travels exactly one copy, so the end frame is pixel-identical to the start and the loop has no seam. sync-marquee.js writes the repeated markup on all sixteen DFW pages. Ten of them load only chrome.css, which carried the single-run animation at 30s — so those ten were driving repeated markup with the wrong model. That plays the copies across the screen one after another, which is the "runs twice", then spends the rest of the cycle carrying the whole span off to the left past an empty bar, which is the "break", and does it in 30s against the other pages' 42s, which is the "faster". Neither animation was wrong; they were paired with the wrong markup.\n\nTHE FIX SELECTS ON data-marquee, the attribute that marks a bar whose run is repeated. It is on all sixteen DFW pages and absent on the Austin calculator, which genuinely holds a single run and keeps the ported Austin behaviour. Keying on the market or on a page list would have been keying on a proxy.\n\nA SECOND DEFECT SURFACED WHILE MEASURING, AND IT WAS ON EVERY PAGE INCLUDING THE ONE USED AS THE REFERENCE. With two copies, the span travels one run per cycle and one run measures about 1296px, so at the end of a cycle only 1296px of bar was still covered. At 1920px that is 624px of bare gold on the right, appearing gradually over the last half of every cycle. The market home did it too; it is the same "break", just smaller, and fixing only the model mismatch would have left it on all sixteen pages. The run is now written four times and the keyframe ends at -25%, so 3888px stays covered at the worst frame — past 3440px ultrawide. Speed is unchanged at one run per 42s, about 31px/s, which is what the market home has always run at.\n\nMEASURED ON THE BUILT PAGES AT 1920px, not reasoned about. A chrome.css-only page and the market home now report the same animation name, the same 42s, the same 5187px span and the same 31px/s. Sampled at five points across the cycle, the span covers the full viewport at every one, and the final frame returns to within a pixel of the first.\n\nTHE REDUCED-MOTION RULE HAD TO BE WIDENED IN THE SAME CHANGE. The new selector carries higher specificity than the bare .ll-marquee span the prefers-reduced-motion block named, so left alone it would have kept the DFW bars moving for exactly the readers who asked motion to stop. Both selectors are now listed, and the gate fails the build if that ever stops being true.\n\nTHE THIRD IMPLEMENTATION IS DEAD AND IS MARKED AS SUCH. .dh-marquee and .dh-marquee-run are used by no page. They are left in place carrying a note rather than deleted, because the note is the record of why there is one marquee and not three. ## Thirty duplicate nav tabs removed from the three file-maintained pages

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reason** | Owner report, Jake Bennett, 18 September 2026: the site has been pushed live to leahylending.com and the DFW pages have a broken navbar; the issue does not appear on staging. |
| **Affected URL(s) or component(s)** | `/texas/dallas-fort-worth/1099-mortgages/`<br>`/texas/dallas-fort-worth/bank-statement-mortgages/`<br>`/texas/dallas-fort-worth/self-employed-mortgages/`<br>`_build/dedupe-nav.js`<br>`_build/check-nav-integrity.js` |
| **Current staging status** | THIS ONE REACHED PRODUCTION, AND IT REACHED IT THROUGH A FILESET THIS BUILD GENERATED AND REPORTED AS VERIFIED. Three pages carried thirty extra "Super Jumbo Mortgages" tabs in the desktop nav, all pointing at the same URL, wrapping the bar into several rows of repeated gold text. Confirmed on the live site rather than inferred: leahylending.com/texas/dallas-fort-worth/1099-mortgages/ served 37 nav anchors, 30 of them identical.\n\nWHY THOSE THREE PAGES AND NO OTHERS. bank-statement-mortgages, 1099-mortgages and self-employed-mortgages are the file-maintained pages: no builder regenerates them. Every other DFW page is written from scratch on each run, so a post-pass that appends twice is erased by the next build. On these three an append is permanent, and repeated appends accumulate. This is the third defect of this exact shape in this project and the first to be visible to the public.\n\nTHE APPEND ITSELF WAS ALREADY FIXED, AND FIXING IT DID NOT HELP. sync-nav-super-jumbo.js used to close the desktop nav region at a </header> that no page in this suite has, so its "is the tab already here?" test read the wrong span, answered no, and inserted again on every run. That was corrected earlier. But correcting an append does not remove what it appended, and the guard cannot see the old rows: it looks for the CURRENT label, "Super Jumbo", while the duplicates carry the label of the day they were written, "Super Jumbo Mortgages". To the guard the nav looked correct, which is why the pass has been reporting success on sixteen pages while three of them were visibly broken.\n\nWHY STAGING LOOKED FINE, which is the question the owner asked. Nothing differs about the two servers. The duplicates are in the HTML file itself — thirty separate anchor elements in the served markup, not something a script adds at runtime — and they were present in the generated upload set, so any host given that set renders them. Staging must therefore be serving an older copy, taken before the duplicates accumulated. That could not be confirmed directly: staging.leahylending.com returns 401 and no attempt was made to authenticate to it.\n\nTHE REPAIR IS A PASS, NOT AN EDIT, because these three files are not regenerated and a hand edit would not survive the next person who runs the build. dedupe-nav.js keeps the first anchor for each destination in the top-level tab row and drops later ones, which makes it idempotent by construction — the property the pass it repairs did not have. It removed 90 anchors across the three pages and a second run finds nothing.\n\nIT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ABOUT SUPER JUMBO. Keying on that label would fix these thirty rows and nothing else; the next renamed tab would accumulate the same way under a different word, on the same three pages. The rule is the invariant instead: in the desktop nav, two top-level tabs may not point at the same URL. The dropdown and the mobile list are left alone — the dropdown legitimately repeats a hub URL a tab also uses, and the mobile list repeats the desktop hrefs by design, so deduplicating across the whole <nav> would empty it.\n\nA GATE NOW ASKS A QUESTION NO BUILDER ASKS. check-nav-integrity.js does not hold a list of expected tabs — a list would need editing on every rename and would be the next thing to go stale. It compares the sixteen navs to each other and names the odd one out, and separately refuses any container that points at one destination twice, which would still fire if every page were broken identically. Negative-tested by injecting a single duplicate: both the gate and the repair pass caught it.\n\nWHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE PREVIOUS SIGN-OFF. The build reported 44 green steps and a verified fileset while this was in it. Nothing was checking whether a nav contained the same link twice, so nothing objected. "0 failed" states how much was checked, not that the pages are correct, and this is a concrete instance of the difference. |
| **Revert path** | Remove dedupe-nav.js and check-nav-integrity.js from _build/build-all.js. The anchors it deleted are not restored by that, and should not be. |
| **Owner approval** | Defect repair, no owner decision required. No copy, claim, destination or form field changed — the surviving tab and its URL are unchanged, and only exact duplicates of it were removed. |
| **Outstanding review or dependency** | ACTION FOR THE OWNER: the three repaired pages need re-uploading to leahylending.com. The rest of the live site matches this build and does not need to be touched, though re-uploading the whole set is harmless. Verified on live before the fix: the hero tiles, the 258 review count, the 25+ footer tenure, the 30s single-run marquee and the GA4 snippet on the Austin shell are all the current build, so only these three files are stale. |

## DFW indexation: production flip prepared, and the crawl path into the cluster reopened

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reason** | Handoff from Eric Bennett, 21 September 2026: Google Search Console reports the Self-Employed DFW page excluded by a noindex tag, and the whole DFW cluster must be audited and made indexable before any further GEO or content work. |
| **Affected URL(s) or component(s)** | `the ten intended-to-rank DFW URLs`<br>`_build/set-indexing.js`<br>`_build/build-dfw-indexation-audit.js`<br>`_build/build-fileset.js`<br>`.htaccess` |
| **Current staging status** | THE CAUSE WAS A MISSED DEPLOY STEP, NOT A DEFECT. "noindex, nofollow, noarchive, nosnippet" is the staging value this project stamps on every DFW page by design. It is removed at deploy time by go-live/set-indexing.js, which rewrites the meta on all 24 pages and installs the matching robots.txt. That step was never run, so the site went live carrying the staging meta and no robots.txt at all — the live one is the SiteGround default.\n\nEVERYTHING ELSE WAS ALREADY RIGHT, measured against the live site with curl before any change: all ten URLs return HTTP 200 text/html with no redirect chain, none sends an X-Robots-Tag, every canonical is self-referencing, robots.txt restricts nothing, and Googlebot and Bingbot get byte-identical responses. Nine of the ten are in the sitemap, which matches the repo copy exactly. The block really was one meta tag.\n\nTHE SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE IS ONE THE HANDOFF DID NOT ASK FOR, and without it the flip would have half-worked. Six pages are held back from the index permanently because they are near-duplicates of Austin pages. One of them is the DFW market home — and measuring the link graph showed it is the ONLY static route into the DFW cluster from the indexed site. Six Austin program pages carry one "Dallas-Fort Worth Options" anchor each and every one points at the market home, not at any of the ten. The Austin React shell's DFW link is injected by JavaScript and is absent from the served HTML entirely: the raw response for leahylending.com/ contains zero occurrences of "dallas-fort-worth".\n\nHeld back under the full staging value, that page also said nofollow. The flip would have opened the ten pages while closing the one door to them, leaving sitemap-only discovery with no internal link signal. The held-back pages now take "noindex, follow" in production and keep the full value in staging. They stay out of the index for the reason they were listed; crawlers can walk through them. noarchive and nosnippet went with the change because both govern how a page is DISPLAYED and a noindex page is not displayed.\n\nThe switch also computed the expected value twice, in two places, from the same constants — apply and verify each doing their own arithmetic, which is how a rule gets applied and then confirmed against a different rule. One function decides now, and the post-write verification calls it.\n\nFOUR DOCUMENTS ARE GENERATED, named as the handoff names them: dfw-indexation-audit.md and .csv, dfw-internal-link-map.csv, dfw-indexation-remediation.md. Everything about the FILES is re-derived on each run from the repo and the upload set, so the report cannot drift from the build. Everything about the SERVER is a recorded curl measurement carrying its date, because a build script cannot re-check a response header and an unlabelled header claim from a constant is how a document starts lying.\n\nTWO EXISTING GATES CAUGHT THE NEW DOCUMENTS ON THE WAY IN, which is worth recording because it is the system working. build-fileset.js refused to build while the four files were excluded from upload/ but not blocked by the .md rule in .htaccess, then refused again while they were excluded but not delivered to go-live/ — "it would reach nobody". Both controls now name them, and a .csv rule was added because nothing had ever covered a CSV at the web root. |
| **Revert path** | Run `node set-indexing.js staging` from the package go-live folder to put the upload set back to noindex. Remove HELD_BACK_PRODUCTION and heldBackValue() from _build/set-indexing.js to restore the full staging value on the held-back pages. Drop build-dfw-indexation-audit.js and its four filenames from build-fileset.js and .htaccess. |
| **Owner approval** | Directed by Eric Bennett in writing, 21 September 2026. Technical only: no URL, slug, redirect, canonical, title, page name, taxonomy or public copy was changed, and no schema or claim was added. Preparing the files is not publishing them — the upload is Jake's action. |
| **Outstanding review or dependency** | TWO THINGS NEED A DECISION BEFORE THIS IS UPLOADED. (1) home-loans is #9 on Eric's intended-to-rank list and is held back from the index by a 9 September instruction, because it measured 84% identical to the Austin /home-loans/ page with both self-canonical. Those two directions conflict; a build script should not pick, so it is declared and reported on every run. (2) Making these pages indexable is the event several LAUNCH-BLOCKERS.md entries were written to gate — the review count, the funded-volume figure and the tenure statement are approved for a noindex staging build and still carry Pending evidence record against an indexable production release. Neither is resolved by this change. Separately, nothing here can confirm Google or Bing indexing; that is Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools after deployment, and the sitemap has never been advertised in robots.txt. |

The surplus is 48px at 1600 and nav width tracks viewport width about 1:1, so the row stops affording one line at roughly 1552. Below that the rule would trade wrapped tabs for an overflowing nav, which is worse.\n\nVERIFIED ACROSS THE RANGE, both page families:\n\n   1919   one line, full 12px spacing, no overflow\n   1600   one line, spread 0, no overflow\n   1560   one line, no overflow\n   1440   tabs still wrap to two lines, nav still 80px, no overflow\n   1024   brand name and tagline each on one line, nav 80px, no overflow\n    375   desktop row hidden, mobile panel unaffected, no overflow\n\n1440 IS NOT FIXED AND IS NOT FIXABLE THIS WAY. The shortfall there is about 100px after the band, and there is no more spacing to reclaim without touching type size, which the owner ruled out when the calculator button was widened. Closing it needs a tab moved into the dropdown or shorter tab wording. |
| **Revert path** | In both stylesheets, put the band max-width back to 1239px, the link gap back to 8px inside it, and delete the 1560-1919 white-space:nowrap rule. |
| **Owner approval** | Owner-directed (Jake Bennett). Spacing only — no label, link, font-size or page content changed. |
| **Outstanding review or dependency** | None outstanding. Still open for the owner, unchanged by this: between about 1240 and 1550 the tabs wrap to two lines. That is a wording or structure decision, not a spacing one. |

## Sticky bottom bar rebuilt to the live Austin bar's measurements (72.7px to 58.1px)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reason** | Owner report, Jake Bennett, 17 September 2026: the bottom pop-up bar and the Schedule Consultation button were taller than before. A first attempt that same day reduced the bar to 60px against chrome.css's --ll-sticky-h and did not fix it, because 60px was not the target — the live Austin bar was. |
| **Affected URL(s) or component(s)** | `/texas/dallas-fort-worth/ (market home)`<br>`landing-assets/home-sections.css` |
| **Current staging status** | THE REFERENCE IS THE LIVE AUSTIN BAR, not a number in our own stylesheets. This bar was rebuilt to Austin’s arrangement on 17 September 2026, so "taller than before" means taller than the thing it copies. Measured on leahylending.com: bar 58px, content row 33.33px inside 12px of padding, Schedule Consultation button 33.33px (text-xs, py-2 px-4, no minimum height), dismiss 24x24. Ours was 72.67px.\n\nTHREE THINGS WERE MAKING IT TALLER, and the largest was invisible.\n\n1. AN UNINTENDED MARGIN, which was the single tallest item in the row. .dh p sets margin-bottom: 1em and scores (0,1,1); the bar’s own .dh-sticky-text scores (0,1,0), so its "margin: 0 auto 0 0" lost its bottom value and the label carried 14.72px of empty space beneath it. In a flex row a margin is part of the item’s margin box: 23.54 + 14.72 = 38.26px, taller than the button, so a margin nobody could see was setting the height of the bar. Selector qualified to .dh .dh-sticky-text, which outranks .dh p.\n\n2. THE BUTTON’S 48px MINIMUM, inherited from .dh-btn. .dh-sticky-cta already carried a smaller font and tighter padding meant to make it a bar-sized button, and that minimum was overriding them — those declarations had no effect on the rendered height at all. Released to 0, which is what Austin has.\n\n3. THE DISMISS AT 44x44, against Austin’s 24x24.\n\nSECTION 17 IS STILL MET, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH READING. The 44x44 minimum interactive target had been implemented by making the boxes 44px and larger, which is what put the two requirements in apparent conflict: match Austin, or meet the target. Section 17 governs how big an area responds to a tap, not how big the painted control is. Both controls now carry an absolutely-positioned pseudo-element, centred on them and at least 44x44, which is part of the control for hit-testing and paints nothing. It is out of flow, so it is not a flex item and does not affect the row. Verified by hit-testing rather than by reading the CSS: a point 4px above and 4px below the button, and 8px above and 8px to the left of the dismiss, all resolve to the control.\n\nRESULT, measured at 1600, 1159 and 375: bar 58.07px against Austin’s 58, button 33.41 against 33.33, dismiss 25.33 against 24, CTA on one line, 16px clear between the two hit areas, no horizontal overflow. Only the market home carries a sticky bar. |
| **Revert path** | In landing-assets/home-sections.css: drop the .dh qualifier from .dh .dh-sticky-text, set .dh-sticky-cta min-height back to 48px, put .dh-sticky-close back to 44x44, and delete the .dh-sticky-cta::after / .dh-sticky-close::after hit-area block. |
| **Owner approval** | Owner-directed (Jake Bennett). Layout only — no copy, claim, link or label changed. No accessibility requirement is waived: the 44x44 target is met by hit area instead of by box size. |
| **Outstanding review or dependency** | None outstanding. Worth knowing: the .dh p margin defect was pre-existing and had nothing to do with the sticky bar's design — any paragraph placed in a flex row inside .dh will do the same thing. Nothing else in the suite currently does, but it is a shape to watch for. |

## Card grids laid out by the number of cards they hold

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reason** | Owner direction, Jake Bennett, 15 September 2026: four boxes should be 1x4 rather than the 3 + 1 orphan the shared three-column rule produced; five should be three on top and two centred below; six stays 2x3. Raised from the Super Jumbo page, where four related cards left a lone card under a full row. |
| **Affected URL(s) or component(s)** | `/texas/dallas-fort-worth/super-jumbo-mortgages/`<br>`/texas/dallas-fort-worth/asset-utilization-mortgages/`<br>`/texas/dallas-fort-worth/no-ratio-mortgages/`<br>`/texas/dallas-fort-worth/construction-loans/`<br>`/texas/dallas-fort-worth/rsu-bonus-commission-income/`<br>`/texas/dallas-fort-worth/bank-statement-mortgages/`<br>`_build/sync-grid-columns.js`<br>`landing-assets/landing.css` |
| **Current staging status** | A post-pass counts the cards in each .program-grid and writes the matching program-grid-N class. A .program-grid-4 rule already existed but had been applied by hand to the one page whose handoff asked for it, so four other 4-card grids kept the orphan; they now pick it up automatically. A .program-grid-5 rule was added: six columns with each card spanning two gives three per row, and the last two are placed at columns 2 and 4 so the pair sits centred across the full grid width rather than tucked under the first two cards.

Counting rather than hand-tagging is the point: add or remove a card and the class follows on the next build with nobody remembering to change it. The pass is idempotent and asserts that every class on disk matches the count on disk, and that a CSS rule exists for every class it writes.

Measured in-browser after letting the reveal animation settle: 4-card grids render one row of four; the 5-card grid renders 3 + 2 with equal 205px gaps either side of the bottom pair; 6-card grids are unchanged at 3 + 3. Tablet collapses to 2 columns and mobile to 1 at every count, with no card wider than its grid and no horizontal overflow. EXTENDED 17 September 2026 to the market home’s own .dh-card-grid on owner direction: its programs section has groups of 5, 4 and 3 cards, and the 5 and the 4 had the same problems. The pass now covers both grid families from one rule, because the instruction is about how many boxes sit in a row, not about which page they are on. Measured there: 6 stays 2x3, 5 renders 3 + 2 with 217px of equal gap either side, 4 renders 1x4, 3 unchanged. REVISED the same day: the owner asked for the market home’s Alternative Documentation group to run as a single row of five rather than 3 + 2. Five no longer means one layout — .dh-card-grid-5 (market home) is 1x5 and .program-grid-5 (the bank-statement page’s five related cards) keeps three on top and two centred — so the build’s summary line is family-aware rather than reporting both as the same thing. Measured at 1440/1280/1024/768/375: one row of five down to 1024 (cards 240px at desktop, 178px at 1024), then 2+2+1 at tablet and stacked at mobile, with no clipped text and no overflow at any width. |
| **Revert path** | Remove sync-grid-columns.js from _build/build-all.js and delete the .program-grid-5 block at the end of landing-assets/landing.css. |
| **Owner approval** | Owner-directed (Jake Bennett, 15 September 2026). Layout only — no copy, claim or link changed. |
| **Outstanding review or dependency** | None outstanding. .tile-grid and .dh-card-grid were checked and left alone: the first is already four across and always holds four tiles, the second holds six on the one page that uses it. |
